column2: On Newsfeeds, Kindness, and the Bodhisattva
Ajahn Kovilo and Ajahn Nisabho interview Ajahn Pasanno for the Clear Mountain Podcast.

column6: Text
I have found your teachings and example of gratitude profound. Could you speak to people who don't yet see the value of gratitude in a Buddhist practice but are inclined towards fault-finding?
We're not autonomous packages of meat.... Trying to prop up the sense of an autonomous individual and personality is really painful and tiring.

I feel like people's interaction with news and the news cycle is a continual drain on [their pool of gratitude]. How would you advise people to work with news and current events so that they can protect their practice and move from that place of gratitude?

You have founded multiple monasteries that balance the traditionalism of Theravāda Buddhism, but Abhayagiri is is connected to the internet and the world. Do you have any advice about how to balance the tradition and living simply with the modern context?
on the timeless teachings of the Pāli Canon.

Can you talk about how to balance the Pāli Canon's emphasis on seclusion (e.g. Snp 1.3: A Rhinoceros) and practicing for one's own benefit with having a relationship with the world? You gave a talk called '[It's About More Than Just Us](https://www.abhayagiri.org/talks/7945-its-about-more-than-just-us).'
It's like people are walking along a road, When they go off to the left, I say, "Go right, go right!" When they go off to the right, I say, "Go left, go left!"|Ajahn Chah
SN 45.2: Half of the Holy Life.
How do we not suffer in any circumstance?

There's talk in the Thai Forest Tradition about _chit durm_, the primal mind or the mind source, and you gave a talk titled '[The Underlying Radiance of the Mind](https://www.abhayagiri.org/talks/7378-the-underlying-radiance-of-the-mind).' Luang Por Sumedho talks about the need to trust in this underlying radiance of the mind. However, there have been times when I've asked you about this type of mind, and you've cautioned not to fool yourself about it.
Ideas are not direct experience.
Analysis on its own is not going to take one to a place of relinquishment and letting go and surrender.

You speak about this determination to align one's life with these values and this vision of Dhamma... So many people have one foot in the monastery and one foot on a banana peel. They've had this insight and see the power of the Dhamma and yet they find themselves in worldly conditions which are difficult. What advice would you give such folk?

I've seen within the monastery the power of sīla and faith beautifully held to clean the heart in ways that a pure focus on technique doesn't manage to.... What is your feeling on that aspect of the path and how it interlocks with Western Buddhism at the moment which is so focused on technique?
MN 8: Effacement.
If you had to give young abbot Ajahn Pasanno two pieces of advice or advise two new monks who aren't actually abbots but are up here in Seattle, what would that advice be?
Can you speak about the dynamics of doing versus being, having projects versus meditating all the time?
MN 108.26: "Meditates, premeditates, out-meditates, and mis-meditates..."
The balance of helping [others] versus looking to one's own practice get conceptualized as the bodhisattva and arahant paths. How do you interact with this common distinction?
To me it's a false dichotomy.
It's hard to keep up with Ajahn Liem.

What is your advice for people who have embarked on this path but have a spouse who does not have the same level of interest? If both partners are deeply passionate about the Dhamma, how can they morph the relationship into a helpful Dhammic partnership?
AN 4.55: Nakulamātā and Nakulapitā.
What is the value of monasteries? What would you say to someone who didn't yet see that value?
